name: Hypothesis Testing
description: Decide whether a result could be luck, and avoid fooling yourself across many tests.

lessonObjectives.l1-could-be-luck: Frame a claim as a null and an alternative hypothesis.
lessonObjectives.l2-measuring-surprise: Compute a $z$ statistic for a sample mean.
lessonObjectives.l3-p-value: Compute a p-value and say exactly what it is a probability of.
lessonObjectives.l4-t-test: Use a $t$ test for a mean and compare it with the $z$ test.
lessonObjectives.l5-two-ways-wrong: Tell type I from type II errors, and trade one against the other.
lessonObjectives.l6-power: Compute the power of a test and choose a sample size.
lessonObjectives.l7-what-p-is-not: Spot the common misreadings of a p-value.
lessonObjectives.l8-two-groups: Test a difference between two means.
lessonObjectives.l9-twenty-tests: See how running many tests produces false discoveries.
lessonObjectives.l10-correcting: Apply the Bonferroni correction and control the false discovery rate.
lessonObjectives.l11-is-sharpe-real: Test a strategy’s Sharpe ratio and adjust for the number of strategies tried.
lessonObjectives.l12-data-snooping: Recognise data snooping, and see why factor research now asks for a $t$ statistic above 3.
